Conversation, family & daily routines

where there’s smoke, there’s fire phrase

also no smoke without fire

classical

Plaut. Curc. 1.1.53 (Lewis & Short s.v. fūmus)
Traupman 258

Semper flamma fūmō est proxima.

Literally “flame is always next to smoke”. In Plautus a warning that the slightest approach to wrong leads to it.
